clue.text: Shakespearian justice was so superficial

definitions.meaning: Justice ... is the country magistrate in Henry IV Part 2 and The Merry Wives of Windsor
lacking depth, of a person or an argument

explanation.surface: A judge in a Shakespeare play is dismissed as lacking any depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the name of a foolish magistrate in Shakespeare, and the everyday adjective for something without depth.

clue.text: 'Abnormal forms of amusement.

parts.note: in biology a mutant specimen is a sport

explanation.definitionFit: Games are pastimes, and biologists call a mutant plant or animal a sport.

clue.text: Feeler put .out before Ann returns

parts.note: to ante is to put up a stake before a hand of poker

indicators.note: something that returns comes back, so the name is read backwards

explanation.surface: A tentative inquiry was put out before Ann came back.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's sensory organ is a feeler.

clue.text: She washes the French négligé

parts.note: la is a French word for the
undress means informal or partial clothing such as a negligee

explanation.surface: A woman washes a French nightdress.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who washes clothes for a living.

clue.text: Full text of part 'of Bloomsbury address

definitions.text: Full text of part 'of Bloomsbury address

parts.words: Full text of part 'of Bloomsbury address
parts.note: Bloomsbury's postcode is WC1, and the clue asks for the two letters spelt out in full

explanation.surface: Someone wants the complete wording of a section of a Bloomsbury speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' sounds like a speech but is a postal address; the London district code WC is the abbreviation expanded.
explanation.definitionFit: The London postal district covering Bloomsbury has the code WC, standing for these two words.

clue.text: Holder of post providing work for time-servers

definitions.meaning: prisoners serving time were traditionally set to sew these sacks

explanation.surface: A postal sack is described as giving occupation to people doing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time-servers' looks like a sneer at idle employees, but it means prisoners: sewing mail sacks was classic British prison work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack for carrying letters, and the item convicts were famously put to sewing in British jails.

clue.text: Wife or mistress so called

parts.note: the courtesy title for a married woman began as a contraction of mistress

explanation.definitionFit: The title used before a married woman's surname, originally short for mistress.

clue.text: Boy: Wordsworth called Myshkin?

definitions.meaning: Prince Myshkin is the hero of Dostoevsky's novel named for this simpleton

explanation.surface: A lad is named by Wordsworth as a Russian prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Both works use the word for a simpleton: Wordsworth's poem title and Dostoevsky's novel about Myshkin.

clue.text: Short measure in pipe but a full glass

indicators.note: the measure sits inside the pipe

parts.note: a brier is a tobacco pipe made of briar root
mm is the short form of millimetre

explanation.surface: Getting a short measure in your pipe, but a full glass of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short measure' looks like a stingy pour but means an abbreviated unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass filled to the very top.

clue.text: Gospel was brought to Aachen on horseback

definitions.meaning: the gospel is literally the glad tidings

definitions.text: was brought to Aachen on horseback
definitions.meaning: Browning's poem How They Brought the ... from Ghent to Aix; Aix-la-Chapelle is Aachen

explanation.surface: Religious teaching was carried by a rider to a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: Aachen is the German name for Aix-la-Chapelle, the Aix of Browning's galloping poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel means glad tidings, and Browning's riders galloped those tidings to Aix.

clue.text: Explosions dislocate start of Tokyo, bus-tours

indicators.note: to dislocate is to put out of place, so these letters are jumbled
the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Violent eruptions disrupt the beginning of a coach trip around Japan's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes T from Tokyo; 'dislocate' rearranges T plus BUSTOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden bursts of anger or noise are eruptions, plural like the clue word.

clue.text: Jones makes one trap turn round

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: to turn the word back means reading it backwards

parts.note: a gin is a snare for catching animals
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A man named Jones makes a single trap revolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jones' defines by its partner name: Inigo Jones, the English architect. 'turn' reverses GIN to NIG.
explanation.definitionFit: The architect Inigo Jones carried this first name, so the surname stands in for it.

clue.text: This down had softening effect

parts.note: put the answer before the word down and the phrase means moderated or made milder

explanation.surface: Something soft and feathery had a soothing effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' seems to be soft feathers or a crossword direction, but it completes the phrasal verb meaning moderated.
explanation.definitionFit: Toning something down means making it less harsh, the softening the clue describes.

clue.text: Qualified mason ?

parts.note: a skilled stoneworker, or a Freemason, whose order is known as the Craft

explanation.definitionFit: A skilled tradesman such as a mason; Freemasonry also calls itself the Craft.

clue.text: .Football club

definitions.meaning: soccer is short for the official name of the ... game

explanation.definitionFit: Soccer's formal name, and a word for a society.

clue.text: Old City address for fishing tackle and line

parts.note: a paternoster is an angling rig with hooks set at intervals along the line
a row is a line of things side by side

explanation.surface: An angler's gear and line give a historic London street address.
explanation.walkthrough: The City here is the City of London; Paternoster Row near St Paul's was the old heart of the book trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic street in the City of London, long associated with publishers, is an address in the old City.

clue.text: Soothing girl in net of deceit

indicators.note: the girl sits inside the rearranged net
a net of deceit is a false or twisted one, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: Mollie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is caught in a web of lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'net of deceit' looks like a web of lies; 'of deceit' is the anagram signal on the three letters, making ENT, and 'in' takes the girl inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream that is softening and calming to the skin is soothing.

clue.text: MP has, gun ruined by moss

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A politician's gun is spoilt by moss growing on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bog moss used by gardeners is a moss genus.

clue.text: Barometer giving false readings, in the kitchen ?

definitions.text: Barometer giving false readings, in the kitchen ?

parts.words: Barometer giving false readings, in the kitchen ?
parts.note: a barometer measures pressure; also a kitchen pan

explanation.surface: A faulty weather instrument has turned up in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'cook' figures is to falsify them, so a gauge of air pressure that cooks its readings is the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealed kitchen pan that cooks food under steam pressure.

clue.text: Oriental festival, third of June

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

indicators.note: the third letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: An Asian festival falls in the third week of June.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the east, as oriental does.

clue.text: German prince voting for imperial preference'

definitions.text: German prince voting for imperial preference

parts.words: German prince voting for imperial preference
parts.note: certain German princes had the right to choose the Holy Roman Emperor, and anyone who votes is also one

explanation.surface: A German nobleman backs a policy of trade preference within the Empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imperial preference' was a British tariff policy; here it means choosing an emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: The princes who chose the Holy Roman Emperor held this title, which also means any voter.

clue.text: Lessen exclusiveness' noticeable in old sectarian:

indicators.note: the letters can be seen inside the first two words of the clue

explanation.surface: Reducing cliquishness was visible in an old religious faction.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an ancient Jewish ascetic sect.

clue.text: Cause of England wearing sackcloth 'only

parts.note: mourning is sackcloth and ashes; England has only the sackcloth because the other side has won the Ashes

explanation.surface: Something leaves England dressed in penitential sackcloth alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket series between England and its old rival; the side that wins holds the Ashes, leaving the loser with sackcloth only.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket nation that beats England takes the Ashes trophy, leaving England mourning without the ashes.

clue.text: Lady runs, up with mount, calling Wordsworth home

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs; the letters reversed across 'Lady runs' are a coincidence of this charade, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: A lady hurries up a hill, calling at Wordsworth's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LADYR. Rydal Mount in the Lake District was Wordsworth's home, so the name with 'mount' calls up his house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lakeland village whose house Rydal Mount was the poet's residence.

clue.text: Foreigners without initial rights

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: aliens are people from another country

explanation.surface: Foreigners are left without basic entitlements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without initial' drops the A from ALIENS.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal claim to hold another's property until a debt is paid, a kind of right.

clue.text: To a great extent Donne is misread'

indicators.note: a misread word has its letters taken in the wrong order

explanation.surface: The poet Donne is badly misunderstood to a great degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is misread' rearranges the letters of DONNE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning hugely or immensely.

clue.text: Breaking-point for Quaker .-no .Roundhead

parts.note: a quaker here is an earthquake, not a member of a religious sect like the Puritan Roundheads; the clue asks where it breaks out

explanation.surface: Something is the limit for a member of the Society of Friends who is no Puritan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quaker' and 'Roundhead' suggest seventeenth-century religion; the dash warns that this quaker is a tremor.
explanation.definitionFit: The point on the surface above where an earthquake starts, where the ground breaks.

clue.text: When to look for letter from Greece

definitions.meaning: the abbreviation for estimated time of arrival
the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone wonders when to expect a letter from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: An expected arrival time, and a Greek letter.

clue.text: It's madness, including £2 for a cigar

indicators.note: the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: mania is a madness
L is the abbreviation for a pound, so two pounds are two Ls

explanation.surface: Spending two pounds on a cigar is madness.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound sign stands for L (from Latin libra), so £2 is two of them; 'including' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot made from Philippine tobacco is a type of cigar.

clue.text: Was' Hazel responsible for Infanta's visit ?

definitions.text: Was' Hazel responsible for Infanta's visit

parts.words: Was' Hazel responsible for Infanta's visit
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme I had a little ..., the King of Spain's daughter came to visit the singer's hazel

explanation.surface: Someone called Hazel may have arranged a Spanish princess's visit.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel looks like a woman's name but is the shrub; an infanta is a Spanish king's daughter, who visits in the old rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazel bears nuts, and the rhyme's tree drew the Spanish princess.
